chunks: A man lodged with the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and remained with him for days. Then he came to him regarding a dispute which he had not mentioned to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Are you a claimant?' He said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You must move out from us, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade that a claimant be entertained as a guest unless his opponent is with him.'

key_terms.تَحوَّل: To move, transfer, or change location — an imperative form indicating a clear command to depart
key_terms.خصم: A party to a legal dispute, claimant, or opponent — the term applies equally to plaintiff and defendant
key_terms.خصومة: A legal dispute, conflict, or litigation — one of the technical terms of Islamic jurisprudence for contested legal matters
key_terms.يُضاف: To be received as a guest, hosted, or entertained — from the root meaning 'to add' (one guest to one's household)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a judge to host one party to a lawsuit without the other party being present?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) upheld prophetic guidance on judicial impartiality by refusing to continue hosting a man who revealed himself to be a litigant in a case. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that a judge must not have private contact with one party to a dispute without the other, preventing any appearance of favoritism. The Prophet's prohibition cited here establishes a foundational rule of procedural justice — equal treatment of litigants — which Imam Ali enforced even at personal expense of hospitality.
word_analysis: the claimant/one party to a dispute
